newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Far East Gold - Physical demand seen emerging.
newsitem.headline: Far East Gold - Physical demand seen emerging.

text.p: Asian gold traders said on Friday their hopes to see the healthy physical demand normally seen in the last quarter had risen as consumers saw an end to the recent price-slide and seasonal buying interest emerged.
Although physical gold demand remained relatively quiet in Friday morning trade, dealers in Hong Kong and Singapore said they were more optimistic about a recovery.

While there were no fundamental incentives pushing gold higher, a senior bullion trader at an international bank's Hong Kong office said there was no discernable trend to gold prices as seasonal physical demand had kicked in, preventing declines.
"There's good demand in Thailand and there's good demand in Taiwan -- it's supporting the market," he said.
Buying from Indonesia and India was picking up mainly because of confidence that spot gold had found a floor at $378 an ounce, Singapore dealers said.

Indian demand, which had virtually disappeared for two-three weeks, should accelerate soon and will probably peak on November 9 and 10, which mark the Hindu calendar's new year, industry sources said.
Hong Kong gold was trading at $381.50/382.00 per ounce at 1230 (0430 GMT), down from its opening price of $381.90/382.40 per ounce.

Singapore and Hong Kong-based traders said they were monitering CRU International's Precious Metals Monitor report that large tonnages of silver had moved through the region over the past seven months, but many said they had not seen any evidence such major movements or unusual activity.
October COMEX metal warehouse stocks released October 10 showed silver stocks had dipped by 2,774,700 million ounces to 131,012,304 ounces.
Silver fixed seven cents higher at US$5.00/02 on October 10 in London.
Thailand and Cambodia took advantage of silver price dips to purchase some metal, Singapore dealers noted.
Demand around the rest of the region for precious metals, however, remained unimpressive and weak, traders said.
"Demand is there, but it's not enormous," a European investment house dealer in Singapore said. "I'm not really seeing much going through."
Gold prices would likely trade in a range of $378-$383 an ounce over the next week, Asian traders said, noting that whenever buying pushed up gold, the metal saw selling.
Dealers said low COMEX silver warehouse stocks in New York had provided support for the rally in silver and that had dragged gold up with it.
"Silver rallied and gold just went with it," said a Singapore dealer.

"There has also been some general shortcovering in the market here, but I'm still a little bit sceptical at the moment. I think silver will fail although you might see it hit $5.02 (an ounce)," he said.
Singapore gold premiums were steady at 30-40 U.S. cents an ounce, with no market news pushing them either way, traders said.
-- Hong Kong Newsroom (852)2843-6358
With a contribution by Rene Pastor in Singapore
